description: Evidence that the ladder/gate F1-F9 test against is itself implemented and unit-tested upstream, in kaiban-distributed@2.0.0's own repository (tests/unit/governance), run via vitest.
notes: npm ci installed cleanly (1036 packages, ~2min) and the governance unit tests ran with no Redis/Kafka/network dependency -- they are pure in-memory unit tests of ActionGate/AuditLog/PolicyEngine/AgentRegistry.

cases: ActionGate.evaluate > disabled => allow with empty verdicts, consulting no validator and recording nothing
ActionGate.evaluate > enabled all-allow => allow + audit called once with the decision and injected timestamp
ActionGate.evaluate > mixed-severity => most-severe action with the deciding verdict first (no short-circuit)
ActionGate.evaluate > ties keep the FIRST-encountered verdict at the deciding severity first
ActionGate.evaluate > enabled with NO validators => allow (empty verdicts) and still records
ActionGate.evaluate > default clock => a string ISO timestamp reaches the audit
ActionGate.evaluate > FAILS CLOSED: a validator that throws yields a block verdict (not a propagated error)
ActionGate.evaluate > stringifies a non-Error validator rejection in the fail-closed reason
firewallValidator > allowed => allow, with the payload built from ctx (taskId from payload)
firewallValidator > blocked => block, reason from the verdict; taskId falls back to agentId
firewallValidator > blocked without a reason => a default reason string
breakerValidator > open => escalate
breakerValidator > closed => allow
costValidator > admit allow => allow; units default 0; default scope without tenantId
costValidator > admit degrade => degrade; uses estimatedCostUnits; default scope WITH tenantId
costValidator > admit reject => block
costValidator > scopeFor override is used instead of the default scope
AuditLog > genesis record has empty prevHash and index 0
AuditLog > links a 3-record chain (prevHash === previous hash)
AuditLog > verifies an untampered chain as valid
AuditLog > verifies an empty log as valid
AuditLog > detects content tampering (mutated decision.action)
AuditLog > detects linkage tampering (mutated prevHash)
AuditLog > returns a readonly snapshot via records()
PolicyEngine > exposes the validator name 'policy'
PolicyEngine > returns the default action with a reason when no rule matches
PolicyEngine > matches a rule by operation alone
PolicyEngine > matches a rule by agentId alone
PolicyEngine > matches by matchAny as a case-insensitive substring of the JSON payload
PolicyEngine > requires ALL provided fields to match (combined operation + agentId)
PolicyEngine > requires ALL provided fields to match (combined matchAny + operation)
PolicyEngine > returns the FIRST matching rule (first-match-wins ordering)
PolicyEngine > uses rule.reason when present, else falls back to rule.id
PolicyEngine > hot-reloads via load() and changes behavior
loadPolicySet > parses a valid YAML string into a PolicySet
loadPolicySet > parses an empty rules array
loadPolicySet > throws when the parsed root is not an object
loadPolicySet > throws when 'default' is missing or not a valid GateAction
loadPolicySet > throws when 'rules' is not an array
loadPolicySet > throws when a rule is not an object
loadPolicySet > throws when a rule is missing a string 'id'
loadPolicySet > throws when a rule has an invalid 'effect'
loadPolicySet > accepts the shipped example policies.yml
AgentRegistry.status > reports 'not registered' for an unknown agent
AgentRegistry.status > reports 'active' for a freshly registered agent
AgentRegistry.status > reports a revocation with its reason (kill-switch)
AgentRegistry.status > uses the default revoke reason 'revoked' when none is given
AgentRegistry.status > reports 'expired' when expiresAt is before the given now
AgentRegistry.status > is still active at-or-after registration when no now is supplied (skips expiry)
AgentRegistry.status > is active when expiresAt is after now
AgentRegistry.status > reports 'invocation limit reached' once the count meets the limit
AgentRegistry.status > treats invocationLimit 0 as unlimited
AgentRegistry.status > reports 'operation out of scope' when the operation is excluded
AgentRegistry.status > is active when the operation is within scope
AgentRegistry.status > ignores scope when no operation is supplied
AgentRegistry.status > records invocations independently per agent
AgentRegistry.status > ignores recordInvocation for an unregistered agent
AgentRegistry.status > ignores revoke for an unregistered agent
AgentRegistry.register (upsert) > clears a prior revocation on re-registration
AgentRegistry.register (upsert) > resets the invocation count on re-registration
AgentRegistry.mayInstantiate > is true for a registered, active agent with selfInstantiation
AgentRegistry.mayInstantiate > is false when selfInstantiation is disabled
AgentRegistry.mayInstantiate > is false for an unregistered agent
AgentRegistry.mayInstantiate > is false once the agent is revoked
AgentRegistry.asValidator > is named 'kill-switch'
AgentRegistry.asValidator > maps an active agent to allow
AgentRegistry.asValidator > maps a revoked agent to terminate
AgentRegistry.asValidator > maps an expired agent to block
AgentRegistry.asValidator > maps an out-of-scope operation to block
AgentRegistry.asValidator > maps an unregistered agent to block
AgentRegistry.asValidator > defaults now to the current ISO time when no opts are given
